confidence_rationale: Landmark Science paper showing that a pre-existing associative schema causally accelerates assimilation of new, schema-consistent traces (one-trial encoding that becomes hippocampus-independent within 48 h). Strong support that schema_fit is a real determinant of how a new trace is integrated. Held at 0.68 because the paper measures consolidation SPEED and hippocampal-independence, not the link-vs-separate allocation decision per se; the schema_fit -> integration-pressure mapping is an inference about a related but not identical operation.
failure_signatures: The paper measures schema-accelerated consolidation (rate of hippocampal disengagement), not the binary allocate-overlapping-vs-separate decision; equating fast assimilation with the gate's integrate output is an inference.
Schema benefit is shown for schema-CONSISTENT items; the paper does not characterize how schema mismatch triggers active separation, leaving the separate-pole of schema_fit under-specified.
Rodent spatial paired-associate task; the schema construct is a learned flavour-place associative structure, narrower than the general schema_fit variable the intake proposes.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Once an associative schema has been learned, new schema-consistent paired associates can be encoded in a single trial and become hippocampus-independent within 48 hours; lesion and learning manipulations show the schema plays a causal role in rapid assimilation of new traces.
mapping.ree_translation: Empirical grounding for the intake's `schema_fit` gating variable: how well a new experience matches a pre-existing structure causally determines how it is integrated (fast assimilation when it fits). In REE this connects to INV-039 (schema-primed rapid assimilation, rate gated by map stability) and supports schema_fit as a legitimate input to the allocation gate -- high fit -> integration pressure toward an existing trace; the control plane could read schema fit to bias overlap.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper operationalizes schema benefit as consolidation SPEED / hippocampal-independence, not as the link-vs-separate allocation choice; mapping fast assimilation onto the gate's 'integrate' output is an inference about a related operation. It evidences the integrate-pole of schema_fit but is largely silent on schema-mismatch-driven separation. The schema here is a specific learned associative structure in rats, narrower than the general schema_fit the intake envisions.
mapping.source_context: Rat; hippocampus-dependent flavour-place paired-associate task with a gradually learned spatial schema; hippocampal lesions at varying post-encoding delays; one-trial new-associate learning.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (Science, causal lesion design, foundational schema-consolidation paper). Mapping fidelity moderate -- it backs schema_fit as a variable and the integrate-pole, but measures consolidation rate rather than the allocation decision. Transfer risk moderate (rat associative schema -> general REE schema_fit term).
